Expected accuracy of individual classification

Source: R/power.R
classification_power.Rd

Simulates animals of each class from the reference allele frequencies of the diagnostic markers, adds genotyping error, and classifies them with classify_hybrids(). The result shows how often each class can be called correctly with these markers, and what it is mistaken for.

Usage

classification_power(markers, n = 1000, error = 0.005, alpha = 0.01, seed = 1)

Arguments

markers

Output of diagnostic_markers() (columns freq1, freq2).

n

Animals simulated per class.

error

Genotyping error rate used to simulate and classify.

alpha

Passed to classify_hybrids().

seed

Random seed.

Value

A matrix of proportions: true classes in rows, called classes in columns. The diagonal is the expected accuracy.

Examples

ex <- hybridclock_example()
mk <- diagnostic_markers(ex$genotypes, ex$groups, "species1", "species2", locus = ex$locus)
round(classification_power(mk[1:15, ], n = 200), 2)
#>               called
#> true           pure1 pure2 F1   F2 BC1_species1 BC1_species2 BC2_species1

#>   BC1_species2  0.00  0.00  0 0.03         0.00         0.83         0.00
#>   BC2_species1  0.01  0.00  0 0.00         0.18         0.00         0.80
#>   BC2_species2  0.00  0.03  0 0.00         0.00         0.14         0.00
#>               called
#> true           BC2_species2 later
